newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court rejects appeal for gold mine closure.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court rejects appeal for gold mine closure.

text.p: Turkey's council of state rejected on Friday an appeal to stop the production of gold at a mine in western Turkey by cyanide-leaching methods, the Anatolian news agency said.
The court said it found no reason to freeze permission for Eurogold, Turkish subsidiary of Australia's Normandy Mining and Posgold, to produce gold in the mine near Ovacik.

"The court's decision is in favour of the continuation of our projects and concludes all the discussion on the closure of the mine," Jack Testard, general manager of Eurogold Madencilik A.S., told a news conference in Izmir, the agency reported.
"Those (environmentalists and villagers) who are against this project now have an important responsibility -- that is to respect state and legal authorities' decisions," he said.
The issue was taken to a higher court after a regional administrative court ruled in favour of Eurogold Madencilik in recent months.
Testard said all measures would be taken around the mine, including treatment systems, to protect the environment and people living nearby.

"Our aim is not to take the gold and leave. We are trying to set up a gold industry here. We want to work jointly with the government to set up this industry for the benefit of all sides involved," he was quoted as saying.

Eurogold secured approval from the Turkish Environmental Affairs Ministry in March to work on the mine after its application six year ago. Approval came after a team of mining experts said the cyanide method would not harm the environment or public health.
Environmentalists have long opposed production in the area, saying the methods to be used by Eurogold would harm local flora and pose health risks.

Bergama township, 12 kilometres from Ovacik, and around 800 nearby villagers had filed a lawsuit requesting an investigation by a new team of experts, saying the first group submitted its report without conducting sufficient research.
